question_bank.stem: A supervised Go learner trained only on historical professional games has a coverage problem because the dataset represents what kind of board space?

options.text: A balanced sample of every legal board configuration
A limited subset of board states humans actually played
A reward-labeled tree of all reachable future games
A complete table of optimal moves for each player

question_bank.rationale: The lecture notes that supervised examples from professional games do not expose the model to the full space of possible Go states, so many strategies and board configurations remain unseen.

distractor_rationales.A: This treats the historical dataset as exhaustive, which the instructor rejected.
distractor_rationales.C: The supervised setup uses move labels, not reward-labeled rollouts for every future game.
distractor_rationales.D: Professional moves are examples, not a complete optimal policy table.

source_ref.evidence_span: You might not see the entire space

frame_evidence.description: Slide titled Motivation shows a supervised Go setup with board state x, selected move y, and a note about the size of the parameter space.

question_bank.stem: In the Go motivation example, a professional player's move is an imperfect supervised target because it is best understood as what?

options.text: A direct measurement of the environment reward
A uniformly sampled action from the legal set
A label produced after evaluating all continuations
A strong human choice rather than guaranteed ground truth

question_bank.rationale: The instructor emphasizes that even excellent human play is not the true optimal label, so supervised learning may imitate suboptimal targets.

distractor_rationales.A: A human move is not the reward signal itself.
distractor_rationales.B: Professional moves are not sampled uniformly from legal actions.
distractor_rationales.C: They are not labels produced by exhaustive game-tree search.

source_ref.evidence_span: even their best game is not the ground truth.

frame_evidence.description: Motivation slide lists disadvantages of classic supervised learning for Go, including missing long strategies and learning by example.

question_bank.stem: Reinforcement learning is motivated when the useful learning signal arrives after a sequence of decisions rather than immediately beside each input as what kind of label?

options.text: A delayed label tied to the outcome of a decision sequence
A static class label attached to each independent example
A segmentation label drawn on every visible object
A shuffled label used only for regularizing the model

question_bank.rationale: RL is framed as learning from delayed feedback after decisions unfold, not from independent input-label examples.

distractor_rationales.B: This describes ordinary supervised learning rather than the RL motivation.
distractor_rationales.C: Visual segmentation labels were not part of the Go/RL motivation.
distractor_rationales.D: The label is delayed outcome feedback, not a random regularizer.

source_ref.evidence_span: learning is all about delayed labels

question_bank.stem: In the agent-environment loop, the agent's interaction at time t is represented by taking an action, receiving an observation, and receiving what other feedback signal?

options.text: A validation loss r_t
A hidden label y_t
A reward r_t
A gradient g_t

question_bank.rationale: The lecture names the observed signal o_t and the reward r_t as the feedback the agent receives from the environment.

distractor_rationales.A: Validation loss is a supervised-learning evaluation metric, not the RL feedback signal.
distractor_rationales.B: A hidden label y_t is not the vocabulary used in the RL loop.
distractor_rationales.D: A gradient is computed during training, not observed from the environment.

source_ref.evidence_span: that we will note ot and a reward rt.

question_bank.stem: In the StarCraft or League of Legends fog-of-war example, the observation differs from the state because the agent receives what view of the environment?

options.text: A reward-only view with no map information
A partial visible view of a larger true state
A shuffled view unrelated to the current state
A full board view identical to chess or Go

question_bank.rationale: Fog of war makes only part of the environment visible, so observation can be a restricted view of the underlying state.

distractor_rationales.A: The agent still observes parts of the map, not just rewards.
distractor_rationales.C: The observation is incomplete, not unrelated to the state.
distractor_rationales.D: Chess and Go were contrasted as fully visible board games.

source_ref.evidence_span: You only see certain parts of the map
